1) fat mass is positively correlated with bone mineral density in the lumbar spine and total hip; 2) fat mass is inversely correlated with bone mineral content in the femoral neck; 3) fat mass is negatively correlated with bone mineral apparent density; 4) fat mass is not correlated with bone mineral area; 5) fat mass is correlated with body weight, body mass index, body fat percentage, and lean mass in the lumbar vertebrae; 6
obesity and osteoarthritis are two diseases with a high degree of comorbidity and that fat mass is a significant predictor of osteoporosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of fat mass on the determination of osteoporosis.
the relationship of body fat mass to bone health, and the impact of fat mass on the determination of osteoporosis.
the effect of fat mass on osteoporosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fat mass has a protective effect on bone, although the magnitude of this effect is still unclear.
fat has a positive effect on bone, but that this positive effect may be offset by the deleterious effects of other factors associated with obesity.
fat mass has a positive effect on bone mass and bone mineral density, but the effect of fat mass on fracture incidence is unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity and osteopenia/osteoporosis are both diseases that affect the elderly population.
the relationship between obesity and osteoporotic fractures is still unclear.
fat mass is a strong and independent predictor of bone mass and osteoporotic fracture in women and men, but the relationship between fat mass and bone is not straightforward.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fat mass should be considered as a covariate when evaluating the association between body weight and osteoporosis.
body fat may be an important component of the body composition that is protective against osteoporosis.
fat mass is a confounder of bone mineral density (BMD) and should always be taken into account in the analysis of osteoporosis.
